title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1 day of sales lost in 7-day week; no prior closure data, but store-level closure reduces demand proportionally.

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Last price increase (2026-09-28) to 4.56 led to 219 units (x0.95 vs baseline); 5.1% increase is similar, so apply x0.95 multiplier.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. The store is closed Monday, removing ~20% of the week's sales. The price is 5.1% above regular, which historically reduces demand; the last price increase (2026-09-28) led to 219 units (x0.95 vs baseline). No promotion or event is scheduled, and the classical model gives no uplift. The closed day is a clear demand reducer. Evidence for price sensitivity is weak but consistent. No noise-adjusted lift from past promotions applies. The median is adjusted downward for the closure and price. Confidence is medium due to limited data on price impact at this level.

TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.8 - 290.0 | 10%-90%: 156.5 - 280.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
